{{Quote|Mythosaurs weren't that big, were they?''"<br />"''Maybe not, but ''they'' don't know that, do they?|[[Bardan Jusik]] and [[Jarkyc]]|<ref name="ImpCom501st">''[[Imperial Commando: 501st]]''</ref>}}
'''Mythosaurs''' were a [[Sentience/Legends|non-sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]] [[Homeworld/Legends|native]] to the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] of [[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore]]. Enormous in size, the mythosaurs dominated their world until the arrival of the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] [[Taung/Legends|Taung]], led by the warrior known as [[Mandalore the First/Legends|Mandalore the First]]. In a campaign to conquer the world for their own, Mandalore the First and his [[Mandalorian Crusaders|crusaders]] slaughtered the gigantic beasts and drove them to extinction. The [[Skeleton/Legends|skull]] of the mythosaur became the symbol of the [[Mandalore (title)/Legends|''Mand'alor'']]—the traditional ruler of all the Mandalorian clans—the planet Mandalore, and of the Mandalorians themselves for generations after.

==Biology and appearance==
{{Quote|Ugly as ''osik''.|[[Ordo Skirata]], upon viewing a mythosaur skeletal replica|<ref name="ImpCom501st" />}}
Perhaps the most notable feature of the mythosaur was its sheer size, so enormous that accounts estimated the creatures to be on par with the scale of a small [[City/Legends|city]].<ref name="TCSWE" /> Four powerful [[Limb/Legends|legs]]<ref name="DCoB">[[Star Wars (1977) 69|''Star Wars'' (1977) 69]]</ref> supported what was surely an impressive weight, for a being of similar size to that of a city.<ref name="TCSWE" /> Some manner of [[Gender/Legends|sexual]] dimorphism was evident between the [[Skeleton/Legends|skulls]] of male and female mythosaurs,<ref name="HotM" /> but in general, the skull of a mythosaur featured large, downturned horns that curved inward toward the creature's jaw, slanted [[Eye/Legends|eye]] sockets, and a mouth that contained a number of long [[Tooth/Legends|teeth]].<ref name="ImpCom501st" /> Mythosaurs also possessed a [[sternum]] composed of rigid [[Bone/Legends|bone]], that was located over their [[Heart/Legends|heart]].<ref name="TBHC">''[[The Bounty Hunter Code: From the Files of Boba Fett]]''</ref>

==History==
===Fall of the mythosaur===
{{Quote|When the ''[Taung]'' Progenitors arrived, Mandalore was inhabited by huge horned creatures—the savage mythosaurs. The clans tested themselves against these great beasts, until all had fallen before their axes and swords.|[[Tor Vizsla]]|<ref name="TBHC" />}}
The Mythosaurs were [[Homeworld/Legends|native]] to a [[Planet/Legends|planet]] in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] uninhabited by any [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]], and thus their great size afforded them dominion over the other creatures who made the world their home.<ref name="HotM" /> The mythosaurs roamed the planet's surface unopposed until the [[Standard day/Legends|day]] when the [[Taung/Legends|Taung]] arrived on the world around the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[7000 BBY]]. Immigrating from the planet of [[Roon/Legends|Roon]], and led by the warrior known as [[Mandalore the First/Legends|Mandalore the First]], the Taung sought to colonize the mythosaur's world as their own.<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> Mandalore the First led a campaign against the giant Mythosaurs, his warriors [[Death/Legends|slaughtering]] the native beasts<ref name="HotM" /> using [[Sword/Legends|swords]] and [[Axe/Legends|axes]] as a test of their skills,<ref name="TBHC" /> until they finally drove the creatures to extinction. The Taung then assumed the name "[[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorians]]"<ref name="HotM" />—or ''Mando'ade'' in the Mandalorian language of [[Mando'a/Legends|''Mando'a'']], meaning "Children of Mandalore"<ref name="TMPaC">{{InsiderCite|86|The Mandalorians: People and Culture}}</ref>—and renamed the conquered world [[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore]] in honor of their leader.<ref name="HotM" />

===Legacy===
{{Quote|Both the mythosaurs and Clan Keldau are long gone, but the skull sigil remains a common symbol of the ''Mando'ade.''|Tor Vizsla|<ref name="TBHC" />}}
[[File:JaingHead.svg|thumb|left|125px|The mythosaur skull sigil]]
Though extinct, the mythosaur lived on as a legendary figure in Mandalorian mythology.<ref name="TCSWE" /> The calcified bones of mythosaurs were used by the ancient Mandalorians to construct their first [[City/Legends|cities]]<ref name="GH15">{{TORcite|type=codex|Galactic History 15: Mandalore}}</ref> and deadly weapons like the [[Mythosaur axe/Legends|mythosaur axe]], which used sharpened plates of bone arranged in a fan shape<ref name="TBHC" /> atop an elongated pole grip. Often considered a ceremonial weapon, mythosaur axes were nonetheless used by [[Mandalorian Crusaders]]<ref name="Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide">''[[Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide]]''</ref> and other veteran warriors in combat for thousands of years.<ref name="FLT">''[[Friends Like These]]''</ref> The skull of the mythosaur became a symbol of the planet Mandalore and its people, none more so than the [[Mandalore (title)/Legends|''Mand'alor'']]—the traditional ruler of the Mandalorian clans.<ref name="ImpCom501st" /> The rigid bone of a mythosaur's sternum was taken from over one the slain creature's hearts, and carved into a [[Mandalore's Mask|ceremonial mask]] for Mandalore the First.<ref name="TBHC" /> The mask was later passed down for generations, worn by each succeeding claimant to the title of ''Mand'alor''. The veteran Mandalorian [[Soldier/Legends|soldier]] [[Canderous Ordo]] was the last known leader to wear<ref name="Revan">''[[The Old Republic: Revan]]''</ref> the mythosaur-bone mask,<ref name="TBHC" /> during his reign as "Mandalore the Preserver."<ref name="Revan" /> Even after the use of the ceremonial mask had fallen out of practice, Mandalorians referred to the metaphorical "[[Crown/Legends|crown]]" held by the reigning ''Mand'alor'' as the ''kyr'bes'', or mythosaur skull.<ref name="ImpCom501st" />

[[File:JaingSkull.png|thumb|left|200px|The skull of Jaing's species served as the initial inspiration for the skull sigil.]]
The image of a skull was taken as the sigil of the ancient Mandalorian [[Clan Keldau/Legends|Keldau clan]], renowned for its [[Instructor/Legends|combat trainers]].<ref name="TBHC" /> While the skull sigil was originally based off of the skull of the renowned combat trainer [[Jaing]],<ref name="SWGTCG">{{SWGTCG|set=Galactic Hunters|cardname=Mandalorian Skull Banner}}</ref> the Mandalorians of later times would interpret the sigil as representing a mythosaur skull due to the striking resemblance [[Jaing's species]] bore to a male mythosaur.<ref name="HotM" /> Another iteration of the skull icon was combined with the insignia of the Mandalorian Crusaders to form the crest of the later [[Mandalorian Neo-Crusaders/Legends|Neo-Crusaders]].<ref name="TBHC" /> The Mandalorian [[Starship/Legends|starship]] company known as [[MandalMotors/Legends|MandalMotors]] also used the skull of the mythosaur as the corporation's logo.<ref name="ImpCom501st" /> In [[Time/Legends|time]], the mythosaur skull became a common symbol in Mandalorian society,<ref name="TBHC" /> used to decorate [[Mandalorian armor/Legends|Mandalorian armor]],<ref name="Hasbro">{{HasbroCite|set=Star Wars: 30th Anniversary Collection|pack=Republic Elite Forces &ndash; Mandalorians and Omega Squad|altlink=https://www.rebelscum.com/tacREFomega.asp}}</ref><ref name="SoR">{{TCW|Shades of Reason}}</ref> equipment,<ref name="VoT">{{TCW|Voyage of Temptation}}</ref> and banners.<ref name="TOR">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]''</ref> Some individuals even chose to don the skull sigil as a [[Tattoo/Legends|tattoo]].<ref name="Orders">{{CWACite|4|Orders (comic story)}}</ref>

[[File:Cityofbone.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The [[City of Bone]], a failed theme park built in the image of a giant mythosaur skeleton]]
In the final [[Standard week/Legends|weeks]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and the early days of its successor state, the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], an [[Hayar's brother|enterprising Mandalorian]] sought to attract adventure tourists to Mandalore to raise a profit. To accomplish his goal, he constructed a large replica of a giant mythosaur skeleton—although its accuracy to scale was debated—on the southern outskirts of Mandalore's [[Capital/Legends|capital]] city, [[Keldabe/Legends|Keldabe]]. The Mandalorian's theme park ultimately never opened, though he, his brother [[Hayar]], and friend [[Jarkyc]], were able to [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|sell]] the defunct tourist site to the Imperial [[Garrison/Legends|garrison]] that had come to establish a base on Mandalore.<ref name="ImpCom501st" /> The so-called "[[City of Bone]]" remained on Mandalore for nearly twenty years, becoming the headquarters of the Imperial [[Slavery/Legends|slaver]], the [[Suprema]], during the Imperial occupation of Mandalore, before being destroyed by [[Fenn Shysa]]'s [[Mandalorian Protectors (Spar)|Mandalorian Protectors]].<ref name="DCoB" />

==Behind the scenes==
Mythosaurs first appeared in the [[Marvel Comics|Marvel]] [[Star Wars (1977)|''Star Wars'' comic]], [[Star Wars (1977) 69|''Star Wars'' (1977) 69]], and numerous sources have featured the mythosaurs and provided information since. However, prior to [[2013]], mythosaurs had never appeared alive in ''Star Wars'', only as skeletons or symbols, primarily as the sigil of the Mandalorian people. That year, with the release of ''[[The Bounty Hunter Code: From the Files of Boba Fett]]''—co-[[Author/Legends|authored]] by [[Daniel Wallace]], [[Jason Fry]], and [[Ryder Windham]]—came the first depiction of a living mythosaur.

[[Abel G. Peña]]'s ''[[Star Wars Insider]]'' article [[The History of the Mandalorians: Exploring the Evolution of a Mighty Race of Warriors|''The History of the Mandalorians'']] introduced both the mythosaur and the [[Jaing]] origins for the [[Mandalorian crest]] and says that the Jaing origin is the truth and that the mythosaur origin is a myth.<ref name="HotM" /> 

The [[Galactic Hunters]] expansion for the [[Star Wars Galaxies Trading Card Game]] also mentions the Jaing origin for the Mandalorian crest, but says that it's frequently mistaken for a [[Bantha/Legends|Bantha]] skull and makes no mention of Mythosaurs.<ref name="SWGTCG" />

''[[The Bounty Hunter Code: From the Files of Boba Fett]]'' only mentions the mythosaur origin for the Mandalorian crest and doesn't mention Jaing at all.<ref name="TBHC" />
